text.p: - The last days before the elections in Chechnya are the most alarming. People are afraid of serious provocations.

- South African diamond group De Beers is not going to give up its business principles for Russia's sake, says the company's representative, commenting on a prolonged conflict between the Russian government and De Beers.
- Amendments to the profits tax law which come into force today are not likely to influence most of Russia's population.

- The information black-out on the NATO Secretary-General's visit to Moscow was initiated by the Russian side unhappy about the publicity surrounding his previous visit to the country, a source at Russia's foreign ministry says.
- With President Yeltsin away from Kremlin, Russia's political elite is beginning to flex its muscles.
- Talks between Russian Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov and NATO Secretary-General Javier Solana started the process of real preparation of a bilateral agreement between the aliance and Russia.
- Reacting to the needs of Russian citizens, Boris Yeltsin has recently issued a tough decree against bureaucrats, says the president's administration.
- Democrats are distorting the memory of Lenin, says the paper in its commemoration of the anniversary of Lenin's death.
- Russian-Belarussian relations develop in sudden bursts of activity which usually end without practical results.
